messages.content: Can you retrieve the weather data for the coordinates 40.7128 latitude and -74.0060 longitude?

function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL and retrieves data as specified by the parameters. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: The URL to which the GET request is sent. It is expected to be a well-formed HTTP or HTTPS URL.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: The Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

headers.description: A dictionary of HTTP headers to send with the request. Each key-value pair represents a header name and its value.

timeout.description: The number of seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up, as a float, or a (connect_timeout, read_timeout) tuple. This is a float type value.

lat.description: Latitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

lon.description: Longitude of the location for the query, in degrees. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters to append to the URL for the GET request.

allow_redirects.description: Determines if HTTP redirections (301, 302, etc.) should be followed.

auth.description: A tuple representing the user credentials for HTTP authentication, typically in the form of (username, password).

cert.description: Path to an SSL certificate file to verify the peer, or a tuple of (certificate file, key file).

cookies.description: A dictionary of cookies to send with the request. The key is the cookie name and the value is the cookie value.

http.description: URL of the proxy for HTTP requests.

https.description: URL of the proxy for HTTPS requests.

proxies.description: A dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy.

stream.description: If True, the response content will not be downloaded immediately but streamed.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate or not, or a path to a CA bundle if verification is needed.

The question: what API endpoint do we use? The tool description says it's a generic GET request; we need to provide a URL. But no specific API is given. Then we can get weather via /api/location/<woeid>/.

But maybe there's a simpler approach: Use the Open-Meteo API: https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast?latitude=40.7128&longitude=-74.0060&current_weather=true. That requires no key. But the param keys might need to match exactly. The function signature expects params dict with keys lat, lon, format. There's no current_weather param defined. But we can still pass arbitrary params? The function definition only lists lat, lon, format. But we could pass other keys? The schema shows optional fields lat, lon, format. It doesn't allow arbitrary keys. So we can't pass current_weather. But maybe we can pass format: "json". But we also need to specify lat/lon. The function signature includes lat, lon, format. So we can set lat: 40.7128, lon: -74.0060, format: "json". That will produce a request to the URL with those query parameters appended. But we need to include the base URL. The function expects a full URL. So we can give "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast" and let the function add lat, lon, format. But we also want to specify additional query parameters like hourly=temperature_2m, but that's beyond the allowed schema. So we may just get minimal data.

Thus we need to find an API that accepts lat/lon as separate query parameters. Many APIs accept lat/lon separately. For example, WeatherAPI.com: https://api.weatherapi.com/v1/current.json?key=YOUR_KEY&q=40.7128,-74.0060. But that needs key.

Open-Meteo seems best. It supports lat/lon. So let's call open-meteo with lat/lon. The function will automatically add lat/lon as query parameters. But we also want to specify format: "json". That's fine.

So we call:

  "url": "https://api.open-meteo.com/v1/forecast",
  "headers": {"Accept": "application/json"},
  "params": {"lat": 40.7128, "lon": -74.0060, "format": "json"}

We might also want to specify "current_weather": true. But the function signature doesn't allow that. However, maybe we can pass it anyway? The schema restricts keys to lat, lon, format. So passing unknown keys would cause validation error. So we can't pass current_weather. So we won't get current weather unless the API defaults to returning something else. According to open-meteo docs, if you don't specify any options, you'll get a default forecast including daily and hourly. But we might not get current weather. But we can at least get some data.

Alternatively, we can use the "open-meteo.com" API with "hourly=temperature_2m" etc. But again, we can't pass arbitrary keys.

Given constraints, we can only pass lat, lon, format. So we can call open-meteo with lat/lon and format=json. That will return JSON with default forecast. That should satisfy the user.
